title: What Is an AI Agent? How AI Agents Work

scenes.narration: You ask a chatbot to set up a meeting, and it writes you a nice message about setting up meetings. But what if it simply set up the meeting? That is the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent. By the end of this video, you will know what an AI agent is, and the loop that makes it work.

A chatbot answers. You ask a question, it writes a reply, and then it waits for you. An AI agent works toward a goal. You tell it what you want done, and it decides the steps, uses tools to take them, checks what happened, and keeps going until the job is finished.

It uses tools to take real steps

cues: An AI agent works toward a goal

scenes.narration: Think of a capable personal assistant on their first day. You say, set up a meeting with Amina next week. A good assistant does not reply with advice. They check your calendar, check Amina's calendar, pick a time, and send the invite. They plan, act, look at the result, and adjust. An AI agent is software that does the same.

visual.title: The assistant analogy
items: Pick a time and send the invite

scenes.narration: Every agent has four parts. First, a model, usually a large language model. This is the brain that reads the situation and decides what to do next. Second, tools. These are things the agent can use, like a calendar, a web search, or code it can run. Third, memory. It keeps track of what it has done so far. And fourth, a goal and rules, which say what to achieve and what is off limits.

visual.title: The four parts of an agent

items.label: Memory
items.sub: what it has done so far

items.label: Goal and rules
items.sub: what to do, what is off limits

scenes.narration: Remember the waiter from our API video? Tools work the same way. Each tool is reached through an API. The agent sends a request, reads the answer, and decides what to do next. A calendar tool, a search tool, a code tool, an email tool. The agent can only do what its tools allow.

Now the important part: the loop. An agent repeats three steps. Think: the model looks at the goal and what has happened so far, and decides the next action. Act: it uses a tool to take that action. Observe: it reads the result and adds it to its memory. Then it loops back to think again. This continues until the goal is done, or until the agent needs to ask you.

Let's follow a real example. The goal: set up a meeting with Amina next week. Think: I need free times for both of us. Act: it asks the calendar tool for your free times. Observe: Tuesday at ten and Wednesday at two are free. Think: now I need to check Amina's calendar. Act: it asks the calendar tool for Amina's free times. Observe: only Wednesday at two works for both. Think: so book Wednesday at two. Act: it creates and sends the invite. Observe: the invite was sent. The goal is done, and the agent tells you.

scenes.narration: You may already see agents at work. Coding assistants that write code, run it, and fix errors. Support assistants that look up your order and process a refund. Research helpers that search many pages and summarize what they find.

visual.title: Where agents show up
items: Coding assistants that write, run, and fix code
Support assistants that look up your order
Research helpers that search and summarize

scenes.narration: Agents are powerful, but they are not magic. They can misunderstand a goal, use a tool the wrong way, or keep going down the wrong path. So well designed agents get only the permissions they need, ask for your approval before risky actions like sending money or deleting files, and keep a log you can check. Treat an agent like a new assistant: helpful, but worth supervising.

visual.title: Limits and safety
items: They can misunderstand or make mistakes
Give them only the permissions they need
Keep a log you can check

scenes.narration: Let's recap. One: an agent works toward a goal, not just a reply. Two: it runs a loop of think, act, and observe, using tools and memory. Three: it needs limits and human oversight.

visual.title: Three takeaways
items: An agent works toward a goal
It needs limits and human oversight
